text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT AND BARLEY SALE - Japan's Food Agency bought 100,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, 30,000 of Canadian wheat, 40,000 of Australian wheat and 20,000 of U.S. barley in its weekly tender. The grain was for September shipments.
CORN SALES - Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group bought 54,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn from Mitsui & Co Ltd Thursday, traders said.

CORN SALES - Morocco bought 46,000 tonnes of corn at $118 per tonne C & F for delivery in two lots in August and September, a Moroccan trader said. The trader said the private AFAC feedstuffs group had purchased 20,500 tonnes for delivery August 10-20 and 25,500 tonnes for September 10-20 arrival.
BARLEY SALE - USDA said private exporters reported sales of 110,000 tonnes of barley to Saudi Arabia for delivery during the 1997/98 marketing year.
SOYMEAL SALE - The CCC bought 1,380 tonnes of soymeal for donation to Guatemala. It paid $283.40 per tonne, FOB, to Archer Daniels Midland Co. Shipment was for July 17-31.

RAPESEED MEAL SALE - Two South Korean buyers groups, the BigFeed Mills and the Korea Feed Association's members in Pusan, jointly on Thursday bought 11,550 tonnes of Indian rapeseed meal at $118.85 a tonne C&F., traders said. The meal was for August 26-September 25 shipment.
CORN TENDERS - South Korean buying group Top Margin Committee passed on offers to buy 52,500 tonnes of corn due to higher than expected prices, traders said.
WHEAT TENDER - The Commodity Credit Corp on July 9 will tender to buy 35,000 tonnes of hard red winter for donation to Tajikistan. Shipment was scheduled for July 23 to August 7.

RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs will receive offers until July 23 to buy 24,000 tonnes of white rice for August delivery, a GEZA spokesman said. Results would be available on July 24.
MARKET TALK - Some Japanese grain importers are buying U.S. corn for October-December shipment, but most are waiting for a better time to buy, local traders said.
... China bought up to 500,000 tonnes of soybean meal from South America in recent days, and more buying was expected on Thursday, traders said.

MARKET TALK - U.S. export opportunities for soybeans are growing after a quick $2.00 per bushel price drop from springtime highs, oilseeds analysts said. "I think what's happened is that the Brazilian basis has firmed up and our price has dropped which makes us competitive from August 1 forward," said Roy Huckabay, vice-president of LIT Investor Services.
